messages.author: 7bdb2cc7d6e9317e
messages.subject: Splitting Dataset by Sex
parts:
Hi all,

I have been able to successfully run analyses on SEM models and I am now trying to run these analyses separately based on sex. I have tried a few different techniques but have not been successful. Here's what I have tried:

1) Model_Fit <- sem(Model, data=interaction, missing="ML", group = "Sex")

When I try to run this function I get the following error.

Error: Error in estimate.moments.EM(Y = X[[g]], Mp = Mp[[g]], Yp = missing.[[g]],  : 
  lavaan ERROR: Sigma_22.inv cannot be inverted

When I try removing the missing = "ML" parameter, I run the following function:

Model_Fit <- sem(Model, data=interaction, group = "Sex")

I then receive the following error:

Error in lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is not positive definite;
  check your model and/or starting parameters in group 1.
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In lav_samplestats_icov(COV = cov[[g]], ridge = ridge, x.idx = x.idx[[g]],  :
  lavaan WARNING sample covariance matrix in group: 1 is not positive-definite
2: In lav_samplestats_icov(COV = cov[[g]], ridge = ridge, x.idx = x.idx[[g]],  :
  lavaan WARNING sample covariance matrix in group: 2 is not positive-definite

2) Because this did not work, I tried separating out males and females within the dataset, as such:

interactionGender <- split(interaction, interaction$Sex)
interactionMale <- interactionGender$male
interactionFemale <- interactionGender$female

After splitting the dataset, I tried running the following to obtain the results for just males:

Model_Fit_Male <- sem(Model, data=interactionMale, missing = "ml")

I still receive the following error:

Error: Error in estimate.moments.EM(Y = X[[g]], Mp = Mp[[g]], Yp = missing.[[g]],  : 
  lavaan ERROR: Sigma_22.inv cannot be inverted

When I remove the missing = "ml" parameter I receive the same error message as above:

Model_Fit_Male <- sem(Model, data=interactionMale)

Error in lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is not positive definite;
  check your model and/or starting parameters.
In addition: Warning message:
In lav_samplestats_icov(COV = cov[[g]], ridge = ridge, x.idx = x.idx[[g]],  :
  lavaan WARNING: sample covariance matrix is not positive-definite

3) I tried recoding my dataset to use 0's and 1's for males and females, respectively, and that did not help solve the issue.

Any guidance as to where I might be going wrong would be much appreciated. Thank you in advance!

Best wishes,
Shubam Sharma

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Splitting Dataset by Sex
parts:
The messages are pretty literal--lavaan finds that the covariance matrix for one group is not positive definite or can't be inverted. Are missing values indicated by "NA" in the dataset? If missing values are indicated by some other code, that may be the source of the problem.

If you don't mention missing data handling procedures, I believe lavaan's default is listwise deletion. Look at the covariance matrix by group using listwise deletion and see if there appears to be a problem.

Thank you for your reply!

All off the missing values are coded as "NA" in the dataset. In the "Sex" column, there are no missing values (only males and females).

I don't think I am able to generate the covariance matrix because lavaan throws the error and does not create the covariance matrix but please correct me if I am wrong (I tried using the inspect command but it could not find the fit object since the SEM function could not run successfully). I tried using listwise deletion with missing = "ml" and even tried using the "default" option for missing but both result in the same errors.

I am a bit confused as to why the model works when both males and females are in the Sex column but when the dataset is limited to just rows where the value in Sex is male or just female, it throws this error.

I tried running a simplified version of the model as listed below and I still receive the error if I try the group parameter or split the dataset by only males or only females:

Model <- '

## Regressions

DV ~ Latent_Variable + Age + Sex 

## Latent variable definition
Latent_Variable =~ Variable1 + Variable2 + Variable3 + Variable4

'

Thank you again. I appreciate your help with this!

messages.subject: Re: Splitting Dataset by Sex
parts: When you analyze the data in a multigroup CFA, the grouping variable itself is not part of the analysis--because it is a constant within each group. So get the covariance matrix for the other variables in the CFA model by group, excluding the grouping variable.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Splitting Dataset by Sex
parts:
On 02/25/2017 06:26 PM, Shubam Sharma wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> I have been able to successfully run analyses on SEM models and I am now
> trying to run these analyses separately based on sex. I have tried a few
> different techniques but have not been successful. Here's what I have tried:
>
> 1) Model_Fit <- sem(Model, data=interaction, missing="ML", group = "Sex")

The canonical way to do this would be to subset your data, as in

Model_Fit <- sem(Model, data=subset(interaction, Sex == "male"),
missing="ML")

If that gives you trouble, something along the lines of:

COV <- cov( subset(interaction, Sex == "male")[,c("x1","x2","x3","x4")] )

where "x1","x2","x3",... needs to be replaced by the variables you wish
to include your analysis. These should be numeric only!

Then, you can inspect this covariance matrix by using

eigen(COV)$values

If all values are positive, then at least the analysis should work for
this group using listwise deletion.

If you keep having trouble, please post the full R script you are using,
and perhaps a snippet of the data.

Yves.
